source_diagnosis.explanation: The fixture opened a metadata-only directory handle. Microsoft's native sharing algorithm does not require such an existing handle to prevent a subsequent delete open: its granted access must contain a read-data, execute, write-data, append-data or delete bit. The directory FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY bit is the corresponding FILE_READ_DATA bit. The absence of an observed refusal in both source and installed phases is consistent with this exact fixture error.
source_diagnosis.inference_boundary: The failed log establishes the missing test refusal and successful propagation of the expected TimeoutError/InterruptedError. It does not identify the holder of the older c31 transient directory lock and does not justify changing process ownership or production cleanup.

primary_sources.section: 2.1.5.1.2.1 Algorithm to Check Access to an Existing File
primary_sources.supports: Existing no-delete-share opens participate in delete conflict only with the listed data/execute/write/append/delete access bits.
Directory listing/read-data is bit 0x1; reading attributes is bit 0x80.
Attribute-access requests are distinct from sharing checks; the fixed directory-handle flags remain appropriate.

repair.after_hunk:
# FILE_LIST_DIRECTORY participates in the native read-data sharing check;
    # FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES alone does not. Share read/write, deliberately not delete.
    # OPEN_EXISTING; directory backup semantics and no reparse following.
    handle = create(str(path), 0x80 | 0x1, 0x3, None, 3, 0x02000000 | 0x00200000, None)
checks_preserved: The fixture uses an actual CreateFileW directory handle on Windows and actual shutil.rmtree; no Windows sharing error is fabricated.
Every removal attempt requires all observed processes exited and their existing native job handles closed.
Every removal attempt requires the real temporary streams and selected helper launch readers closed.
The real first sharing refusal must be observed before the handle is released.
The same owned directory must be retried at least twice, then removed.
Both original deadline and explicit cancellation exceptions must survive successful cleanup.
The deadline, bounded join, total duration, no-output, no-stage and cleanup-error assertions remain byte-identical.
All existing case identities, gate Counters and production process/manifest/cache behavior remain unchanged.
